title: AZFinText
summary:
AZFinText (Arizona Financial Text System) is a textual-based quantitative financial prediction system written by Robert P. Schumaker of University of Texas at Tyler and Hsinchun Chen of the University of Arizona. This system differs from other systems in that it uses financial text as one of its key means of predicting stock price movement.

AZFinText overcomes information lag-time limitations by utilizing the terms used in financial news articles to predict future stock prices twenty minutes after the news article has been released. It works by ingesting large quantities of financial news stories along with minute-by-minute stock price data. It then buys or shorts every stock it believes will move more than one percent of its current price in the next twenty minutes and it never holds a stock for longer.

Each financial news article is represented using three textual analysis techniques: Bag of Words, Noun Phrases, and Named Entities. It was found that using the article terms and the price of the stock at the time the article was released was the most effective model, and using proper nouns was the most effective textual representation technique. It is believed that certain article terms can move stocks more than others, and AZFinText capitalizes on the arbitrage opportunities that exist when investment experts over- and under-react to certain news stories.

Sector-based training was found to be most effective, netting an 8.50 percent trading return, outperforming several well-known financial advisors during the study period. The researchers investigated 9,211 financial news articles and 10,259,042 stock quotes covering the S&P 500 stocks during a five-week period, applying analysis using a Support Vector Machine derivative. Using momentum and contrarian stock portfolios, AZFinText netted a 20.79 percent return during the study period.
